note.after_visit_summary: Today we looked at your warts and the rough bumps on your arms. The warts are common and caused by a virus. We froze them with liquid nitrogen to help them go away. The rough bumps on your arms are called keratosis pilaris, which is harmless and common in kids. For the warts, they may get red, form a blister, or turn dark over the next few days. If they are sore, you can take children's acetaminophen as directed on the package. Once the blisters heal in about a week, start using the 17 percent salicylic acid liquid every night: soak the wart, file off the dead skin with your own emery board, then cover it with duct tape. Keep using the 10 percent urea cream on your arms once a day after bathing to smooth the rough bumps. Try not to pick or bite the warts, as this can spread them. You can go to school and play sports as normal. If a wart becomes very red, swollen, or has pus, call the clinic. We will see you back in 3 to 4 weeks to check the warts and possibly freeze them again.
